answer: Each agent may submit only one claim per interval, and claims are settled against a public randomness beacon after a challenge window. To earn standing, an agent must escrow a bond that is slashed if its claim conflicts with evidence later verified by peers; repeated claims cannot multiply influence because weight is capped per interval. A Sybil attacker must therefore lock capital in every identity and risk losing it, rather than gaining power by cheaply minting accounts. The cedar, kernel, and lotus agents face the same rule.
